import { defineTable, col, rel } from "@rebasepro/server/schema";
import { issues } from "./issues";
import { users } from "./users";

// ⚠ Not reproduced exactly by `rebase db push` — read before pushing:
//   - "category" is a varchar with no length, declared as text: a push would convert it to text, which keeps every value.
//   - "created_at" is timestamp without time zone, declared with `col.custom()`: Rebase serves it as the driver returns it, and `rebase db generate` / `db push` refuse it until the planner can plan a custom type (`custom-sql-type`).
//   - "updated_at" is timestamp without time zone, declared with `col.custom()`: Rebase serves it as the driver returns it, and `rebase db generate` / `db push` refuse it until the planner can plan a custom type (`custom-sql-type`).
export const reports = defineTable("reports", {
    columns: {
        id: col.serial().primaryKey(),
        issueId: col.integer().notNull(),
        userId: col.integer().notNull(),
        details: col.text().notNull(),
        category: col.text().notNull(),
        createdAt: col.custom("timestamp without time zone").notNull(),
        updatedAt: col.custom("timestamp without time zone").notNull()
    },
    relations: {
        issue: rel.belongsTo(() => issues, { onDelete: "no action" }),
        user: rel.belongsTo(() => users, { onDelete: "no action" })
    },
    rls: "admin-only"
});
